newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June import prices rose 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June import prices rose 0.4 pct.

text.p: Labor Department report of U.S. import and export price changes by percent (unadjusted).
The department reported June price indexes (1995 base year equals 100) of 98.7 for both imports and exports.

The 0.4 percent rise in import prices in June was the first increase since a 0.3 percent rise in December, the Department said. The rise in non-petroleum import prices was also the first increase since December, when they rose 0.1 percent.
The 0.5 percent rise in import prices for automotive vehicles, parts and engines was the largest rise since May 1995 when they were also up 0.5 percent.

Capital goods import prices rose for the first time since September and for the third time in the past two years, the department said. Labor attributed the turnaround in capital goods import prices to the strengthening of foreign currencies versus the dollar.
Export prices fell for the third month in a row, a trend attributed to falling agricultural export prices, the department said.
